description: We care about turning NASA Earth observations, soil information, crop traits, and farmer priorities into a clear decision-support tool for rotation strategies that support soil health and climate adaptation.
summary:
KinField is a geospatial crop rotation decision-support platform built for the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge. Instead of offering opaque AI guesses, KinField lets farmers and extension agronomists pin or draw any field on an interactive dark satellite map and backtest 3 crop rotation strategies across 20 years (2005–2024) of real daily NASA POWER agroclimatology.

Using a deterministic FAO-56 soil-water bucket and solar-calibrated Hargreaves–Samani evapotranspiration model, KinField calculates yearly water stress, flowering heat spikes, frost risk, and groundwater overdraft. Farmers can inspect NASA GIBS MODIS, SMAP soil moisture, and GPM rainfall layers over seasonal timelines, test "+0–3°C warming" and "±30% rain" climate scenarios, and see exact uncertainty and data-resolution limits. By turning complex satellite climate series into clear 20-year pass/fail timelines, KinField helps protect long-term soil health, conserve groundwater, and reduce seasonal crop failure.
details:
WHAT KINFIELD DOES & HOW IT WORKS

KinField is a farmer-first geospatial decision-support tool that replaces black-box crop advice with transparent, 20-year historical climate backtesting.

1. Interactive Satellite Field Selection: Farmers open a dark-graded satellite map (keyless Esri World Imagery with clear white road/village labels), locate their plot via village/district search, GPS ("My Location"), district quick-pins, or polygon boundary drawing (calculating exact area in hectares and acres).

2. Live NASA Earth Observation Context Layers: Users toggle NASA GIBS WMTS layers — MODIS Terra True Color (250 m), SMAP L4 Root-Zone Soil Moisture (~9 km), and GPM IMERG Precipitation (~10 km) — and scrub across seasonal dates (Monsoon Peak, Post-Monsoon, Rabi Grain-Fill, Bare Soil) to visually inspect vegetation stress and moisture transitions.

3. Deterministic 20-Year Backtest Engine (No Black-Box LLM in Scoring): When the farmer selects their current crop, irrigation access (Rainfed / Limited / Full), equipment level, and up to 2 priorities (Save Water, Income, Soil Health, Stability), the backend loads 7,305 days (2005–2024) of real NASA POWER agroclimatology (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, PRECTOTCORR, GWETROOT, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN) plus ISRIC SoilGrids / regional Available Water Capacity (AWC).

4. Biophysical Crop-Water & Stress Simulation: Daily reference evapotranspiration (ET0) is computed via solar-calibrated Hargreaves–Samani and routed through a 4-stage FAO-56 Kc root-zone soil-water bucket (including rice paddy percolation loss). Each year (2005–2024) is flagged GOOD, MODERATE, or FAILED if seasonal water satisfaction drops below tolerance, flowering-window Tmax triggers heat spike damage, Tmin trips frost thresholds, or irrigation extraction causes groundwater overdraft.

5. Transparent Tradeoffs & Climate What-If Testing: KinField always compares the farmer's Current Practice against 2 priority-aligned rotation strategies (incorporating nitrogen-fixing legumes, deep-rooting millets, cover crops, or water-saving shifts). Interactive Rainfall (±30%) and Warming (+0–3°C) sliders re-rank strategies live. Every output displays safe years out of 20, water use (mm), soil organic/nutrient score, income proxy, dataset spatial resolution limits, confidence level, and a clear Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) extension disclaimer.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & ARCHITECTURE

- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Leaflet, Motion, Lucide Icons

- Backend: Node.js 22, Express, tsx (single-port architecture serving REST API + SPA)

- Scientific Datasets & Services: NASA POWER Daily Agroclimatology API (with pre-seeded real 2005–2024 grid files for Hisar, Ludhiana, and Aurangabad), NASA GIBS WMTS, ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 REST API, OpenStreetMap Nominatim Geocoding, and Open-Meteo Elevation API.

CREATIVITY, BENEFITS & HUMAN-CENTERED DESIGN FACTORS

- Honest Separation of Visualization vs. Modeling: KinField explicitly tells users which NASA layers are visual map context (MODIS, SMAP L4, GPM) versus direct numerical model inputs (NASA POWER + SoilGrids), preventing misleading claims about field-scale precision from ~9–50 km grid cells.

- Speed & Offline Resilience: Pre-seeded NASA POWER datasets and 0.25° grid caching keep backtests under 2 seconds, with deterministic fallback behavior if upstream APIs time out.

- Supporting Local Expertise: KinField frames satellite history as climate odds—reminding farmers to verify soil salinity, borewell yield, and local varieties with KVK agronomists.

SI / AI DEVELOPMENT DISCLOSURE

While the live agronomic simulation and ranking engine inside KinField is 100% deterministic (zero LLMs or black-box predictions in scoring), Super Intelligence (SI) tools were used during software engineering to assist with React/TypeScript code scaffolding and to generate the dark orbital farmland background image on the landing screen.
